matches.why: Buy only the best, highest-quality business models; same idea as RB1.
Operating leverage, margins can go much higher; RB13 is operating leverage with margins rising.
Buy part, low reinvestment need; RB14 capital light, reinvestment preferably zero (defensive deals also RA11).
Avoid part; no avoid rule on coerced use. Same idea appears only in buy form (RB8).
Natural monopolies or oligopolies; RB7 dominance by monopoly/oligopoly, RB8 'natural'.
No card price rule on rejecting sum-of-the-parts; RP1 (DCF) is a different idea.
Process: study and follow a company for many years before acting; RO4.
Price drops/volatility used as entry into great businesses; RP8 entry on a scare-driven drop.

contradictions.why: Interest was triggered by FICO's 2018 pricing change, a sudden change; RB10 requires pricing power as a long-running pattern, 'not a sudden change', a decade plus. Card lists FICO as a fit without recording this exception.

FICO had not raised prices for 25 years before 2016, so it had no decade-plus record of above-inflation price rises when bought; opposite of RB10's number. Not recorded on the card (section 5 mentions the mortgage score +100% only under C13).

He bought on a change in the growth profile 'others ... may not have realized'; RB6 says extrapolate a long record, 'not a predicted step change'. Card C15 closes only record length ('not every company'), not acting on a change.
